claims.text: The proposed model separately computes lattice and electronic heat transport using atomistic simulation and machine-learning corrections.
The proposed model incorporates local lattice distortion, atomic-mass disorder, force-constant fluctuations, and temperature-dependent anharmonicity.
The HfNbTaTiZr specimen contains a controlled 1 wt.% oxygen impurity.
HfNbTaTiZr exhibits complex local lattice distortions.
The relevant 1 wt.% oxygen specimens have minimal defect concentrations comparable to the experimental specimens.
Local lattice distortions and force-constant fluctuations mediate phonon scattering independently of electronic transport.
Static disorder arising from atomic-mass and force-constant variability and dynamic anharmonic vibrations influence lattice heat transport.
Accounting for static and dynamic disorder permits the intrinsic phononic thermal conductivity to be decoupled from the electronic contribution.
The proposed model will predict HfNbTaTiZr lattice thermal conductivity within approximately 10% over 200–1200 K.
The proposed model will outperform Debye-temperature-based and defect-free-crystal approaches.
Combining the predicted lattice conductivity with a separately measured electronic contribution will reproduce total conductivities of 10–17 W/(K·m).
Earlier analytical approaches assume perfect, defect-free crystals and rely on Debye-temperature estimates.
Earlier approaches omit local structural complexity and consequently have larger prediction uncertainties.
The claimed predictive performance applies to high-purity HfNbTaTiZr with controlled oxygen content between 200 and 1200 K.
Below 200 K, lattice and electronic heat-transport contributions are comparable.
Possible quantum effects and uncertain electron–phonon coupling limit model applicability below 200 K.
Diffraction or scattering measurements can assess local lattice distortion in the test specimens.
A deviation greater than ±10% in lattice thermal conductivity above 200 K would falsify the hypothesis.
